classification.difficultyReason: Select the relevant straight-line, revolution or right-angle sum from each diagram; the hardest parts combine adjacent or vertically opposite angles with a short linear equation.

content.prompt: This question reviews angles at a point. Find the angles marked with pronumerals, giving reasons.

spec.description: Three rays from A with endpoint labels B, C and D; right-angle square between AC and AD.
spec.mathematics: Angle BAD is 135 degrees; angle CAD is 90 degrees; angle CAB is theta.

answer.worked:
Angles in a revolution add to $360^{\circ}$.
$$\begin{align*}\theta+135^{\circ}+90^{\circ}&=360^{\circ}\\\theta+225^{\circ}&=360^{\circ}\\\theta&=135^{\circ}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Straight lines AB and PQ intersect at M; all four endpoint labels and three angle labels retained.
spec.mathematics: AMQ is alpha; PMA is beta; QMB is 110 degrees.

answer.worked:
Vertically opposite angles are equal, so $\beta=110^{\circ}$.

Adjacent angles on a straight line are supplementary.
$$\begin{align*}\alpha+110^{\circ}&=180^{\circ}\\\alpha&=70^{\circ}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: K, N and L are collinear; NR and NS form a marked right angle above the line.
spec.mathematics: KNR is alpha; RNS is 90 degrees; SNL is three alpha.

answer.worked:
Adjacent angles on a straight line add to $180^{\circ}$.
$$\begin{align*}\alpha+90^{\circ}+3\alpha&=180^{\circ}\\4\alpha&=90^{\circ}\\\alpha&=22\tfrac12^{\circ}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: AD and BE are straight lines through N, with additional ray NC and a right-angle square between NB and NC.
spec.mathematics: BNC is 90 degrees; CND is 60 degrees; ANE is theta and vertically opposite BND.

answer.worked:
$\angle BND=90^{\circ}+60^{\circ}=150^{\circ}$.

Vertically opposite angles are equal, so $\theta=150^{\circ}$.

spec.description: Five unlabelled rays and five consecutive theta labels around their common vertex; source ray directions are schematic.
spec.mathematics: Five equal angles partition one revolution.
spec.answerVisibility: Unknown labels only; no calculated value.

answer.worked:
Angles in a revolution add to $360^{\circ}$.
$$\begin{align*}5\theta&=360^{\circ}\\\theta&=72^{\circ}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: OP and OS bound a marked right angle, containing rays OQ and OR in that order.
spec.mathematics: POQ is three alpha; QOR is two alpha; ROS is alpha; POS is 90 degrees.

answer.worked:
The three adjacent angles form a right angle.
$$\begin{align*}3\alpha+2\alpha+\alpha&=90^{\circ}\\6\alpha&=90^{\circ}\\\alpha&=15^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
